steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Climate change is one of the greatest global challenges, caused by greenhouse gas emissions from burning fossil fuels. The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to limit warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The UK has committed to net zero carbon emissions by 2050 — the first major economy to do so. This requires transforming energy, transport, and industry. The Climate Change Committee monitors progress.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Extreme poverty has declined globally but inequality persists both between and within nations. The richest 1% own nearly half the world's wealth. Global cooperation on trade, aid, and debt relief is essential.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) set 17 targets for a better world by 2030, including: no poverty, zero hunger, quality education, gender equality, clean water, climate action, and reduced inequalities.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What are the UN Sustainable Development Goals? | Q: Explain why climate change requires international cooperation. | Q: Evaluate the effectiveness of individual actions vs government policy in addressing sustainability.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always link sustainability to the three pillars: economic, social, environmental Use specific SDG numbers and names when referencing them (e.g. SDG 13: Climate Action) When evaluating climate action, consider both mitigation (reducing emissions) and adaptation (preparing for effects)
